Subject: MSA + Order Form: liability cap & termination refund (ACME-119)

Neha / Lauren,

Thank you for the draft MSA and the order form. A few high-level items we need addressed before procurement can move forward:

1) Limitation of Liability: ACME cannot accept a broad liability cap that excludes data/privacy incidents. We propose a carve-out for breaches involving ACME personal data and regulatory fines. Our initial ask is $100k cap for general liability with an explicit carve-out for data/privacy up to $5M.

2) Consequential Damages: Please confirm that consequential damages are excluded, but we need a carve-out for third-party claims arising from data breaches.

3) Termination & Refunds: If ACME terminates for convenience within the first 12 months we expect a refund of prepaid fees for unused months. Alternatively, if Redwood proposes no refund, we will require significant wind-down assistance to transition away (minimum 40 hours).

4) Wind-down Assistance: We want explicit language in the order form that guarantees assistance hours, response times, and deliverables.

Can you circulate a redline that shows Redwood's position on the three buckets above? Procurement needs a clear commercial position before we pull legal in. Happy to set a short call if that helps.

Best,

Jenny Morales
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
ACME Corp

Neha / team —

Quick legal position and suggested redline bullets (high level):

1) Limitation of Liability (LoL): Recommend tying the cap to the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months; or (ii) $500,000. That is commercially defensible and limits open exposure while giving ACME a meaningful recovery. Avoid an open-ended $5M carve-out for all data incidents — instead, carve out only for willful misconduct and gross negligence. For data/privacy breaches, make a separate negotiated remedy bucket with caps and mutual cooperation obligations (i.e., incident response/playbooks, forensic costs).

2) Consequential damages: Keep the general exclusion of consequential damages but permit third-party claims directly resulting from Redwood's material failure to protect customer PII; those claims should be recoverable up to an agreed-upon cap (suggest $2,000,000 limited to PII exposure). This is narrower than ACME's proposed unlimited carve-out but addresses their core concern.

3) Termination for Convenience and Refunds: We should avoid an unconditional full refund. Propose pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for unused whole months, less documented non-recurring setup costs, with an explicit cap (e.g., no refund to exceed prepaid fees). For early termination in the first 90 days, consider a 75% refund of unused prepaid as a limited commercial concession.

4) Wind-down Assistance: Accept a defined number of assistance hours (40 hours as requested) with standard hourly rates or a fixed credit. Put firm SLA/deliverable commitments in the Order Form and cap total hours (e.g., 40 hours included, additional hours billed thereafter). 

5) Practical edits: Add set-off and survival clauses, include explicit timelines for invoices/credits, and ensure the redline contains an integration clause between the MSA and Order Form.

I will draft targeted language for the LoL and termination sections and attach a proposed redline by EOD. For commercial numbers (cap amounts / refund percentages) sync with Lauren.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Jenny —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is our consolidated counterproposal and a redline (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx) that contains the specific edits. High-level summary of our positions below so procurement/legal can react quickly: 

• Limitation of Liability: Cap will be the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (b) $500,000.
• Data/PII Exposure: We will carve out third-party claims resulting from Redwood's material failure to protect PII with a capped remedy of $2,000,000 and mandatory incident response cooperation (forensic costs, notification support). Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain uncapped, subject to proof.
• Consequential Damages: Still excluded broadly; carve-out limited to third-party claims tied directly to PII exposure as above.
• Termination for Convenience: Pro-rata refund of unused whole months of prepaid fees (calculated monthly), less documented non-recurring setup costs. For terminations in the first 90 days, offer a one-time 75% refund of unused prepaid as a gesture.
• Wind-down Assistance: 40 hours included at no charge (deliverables: data export in agreed format, KV cache snapshot, two 1-hour KT sessions, and a runbook). Additional hours billed per standard PS rates.

We think this is a fair compromise between ACME's risk concerns and Redwood's commercial needs. If ACME prefers a phone call, we're available Tue 11:00 PT — otherwise please provide redline comments by Wed EOD and we'll iterate.
